name: Berkeley School District
notes: Seed confirmed and refined. The Eighth Circuit (515 F.2d 1365) states the Berkeley district was established in 1937 when Kinloch School District No. 18 was split in two, 'Berkeley district being white and the new Kinloch black.' The City of Berkeley incorporated July 30, 1937 with boundaries drawn to include only white families (barkerreunion.blogspot.com, citing John A. Wright Sr.; Wikipedia 'Kinloch High School'); some secondary sources date the completed split to 1938. Per the seed note, the new district took over the white Kinloch High School (Hancock Avenue building), renamed Berkeley High School. The district annexed the Scudder School District on Aug 24, 1960 (Southern School News, Oct 1960) and took in Robertson students when that high school closed in 1964 (Wikipedia 'Berkeley High School (Berkeley, Missouri)'). On June 7, 1975, the U.S. District Court (Judge James H. Meredith) ordered Berkeley and Kinloch annexed to Ferguson-Florissant R-II (388 F. Supp. 1058; SHSMO Kinloch School Desegregation Collection S0707). Member schools incl. Berkeley High School (ALL-114; Hancock, Caroline Ave, and Walter Ave campuses), Hancock School/'Little Red Schoolhouse' (5924 Hancock), Airport Elementary (built 1954, ALL-390), the former Berkeley HS turned Berkeley Middle turned Berkeley Intermediate (8300 Frost Ave), and Holman Elementary (8811 Harold Dr).

name: Berkeley School District Elementary System
school_type: Public Elementary (district aggregate, not a single school)
notes: PSEUDO-ENTITY FLAG: this row is an aggregate of the Berkeley district's elementary schools, not a real named entity — kept as a search alias per no-delete rule, but Track B should not search it directly. The Berkeley district's elementary-level schools included Hancock School ('Little Red Schoolhouse', 5924 Hancock Ave — the 1902 white Kinloch School building, which housed both elementary and high school students in 1935 per the John A. Wright Sr.-based history at barkerreunion.blogspot.com); Airport Elementary (8429 Airport Rd, built 1954 — ALL-390/ALL-408); and later Berkeley Elementary/Intermediate (8300 Frost Ave, still operating under FFSD) and Holman Elementary (8811 Harold Dr, Berkeley — still operating; may be a post-1975 building, unverified). Whether the Berkeley district operated any all-Black elementary before annexing Scudder (1960) and Robertson (1964) is undetermined — the 1937 split left the Black schools in Kinloch, and Scudder/Robertson brought their own buildings. Reconstructing the full member-school list needs district records not found online; recommend human follow-up with FFSD administrative records or the St. Louis County library history collections.

name: Kinloch School District
notes: Seed's 1902 formation confirmed: at the 1902 annual spring meeting of the Ferguson School District, white residents of the Kinloch area voted to split and form their own district; a Board of Arbitration appointed by the County Superintendent ordered the creation of 'Kinloch School District No. 5, Township 46, Range 6 East' (barkerreunion.blogspot.com, quoting the ruling via John A. Wright Sr.). The district was renumbered Kinloch School District No. 18 in 1910. Seed's 'from parts of Ferguson and Scudder' is partially verified — the split came from the Ferguson district; the Scudder Avenue School (a pre-existing building) became Kinloch's Black elementary. Segregated per Missouri law: one high school and one elementary for whites, one elementary (Dunbar, est. ~1913-14) for Black children. Split in 1937-38 into the white Berkeley district and the all-Black Kinloch district despite Black residents' opposition; the all-Black district's 'separate but equal' Kinloch High School opened 1938 and ran to ~1976 (Wikipedia 'Kinloch High School'). After the 1971 DOJ suit and Liddell litigation, the U.S. District Court ordered annexation to Ferguson-Florissant on June 7, 1975 (388 F. Supp. 1058); upheld by the Eighth Circuit (515 F.2d 1365). Member schools incl. Kinloch High School (ALL-393/497), Dunbar School (ALL-395, the longest-operated all-Black school, closed 1975), Kinloch Elementary (ALL-508). ZIP corrected from seed's 63134 to 63140 (Kinloch).

name: Scudder School District
district_operator: Scudder School District (to 1960); Berkeley School District (after 1960)
notes: Seed's closure confirmed: the Berkeley School District voted to annex the Scudder School District on August 24, 1960 (Southern School News, October 1960, p. 14 — reducing St. Louis County's regular districts to 28). Scudder then had ~260 pupils, ~75% Black, and no high school; its high-school-age children were tuitioned to Soldan High School in St. Louis. Formation date not found — the 'Fairmont District No. 17' alias suggests a renamed 19th-century township district (seed's '1800s' is plausible but unverified). The district name relates to the Scudder area/avenue near Kinloch Park, but the 'Scudder Avenue School' (ALL-392) belonged to the Ferguson/Kinloch lineage, not necessarily this district — treat as a naming overlap, not a confirmed member school. Member school building(s) undetermined.

name: Ferguson-Florissant School District
historical_names: Ferguson Reorganized School District R II
notes: SEED ERROR: seed gives 1938, but Ferguson-Florissant R-II was created by the October 1951 county reorganization vote that consolidated the Ferguson, Florissant, and St. Ferdinand districts (PRiME Center/SLU; Eighth Circuit 515 F.2d 1365: 'in 1951 Ferguson, Florissant and St. Ferdinand School Districts reorganized'). The merger took effect for the 1952 school year (Living New Deal). Seed's 1938 may conflate the predecessor Ferguson Public School District or the 1939 opening of Ferguson High School. The district annexed Berkeley and Kinloch by federal court order June 7, 1975. Currently operating ~22 schools across 11 municipalities; headquarters 8855 Dunn Rd, Hazelwood (fergflor.org; NCES district 2912010). Yearbooks belong to member schools, not the district.

name: Mark Twain School
historical_names: Mark Twain Restoration and Re-Entry Center
notes: SEED ERROR: 'Berkeley area' is wrong — the Mark Twain institution is in the Hazelwood/Florissant part of the district, now at 8855 Dunn Rd, Hazelwood MO 63042 (same address as district HQ), serving FFSD middle/high students as the Restoration & Wellness Center (rwc.fergflor.org). A Florissant municipal crosswalk ordinance also places 'Mark Twain School' on Derhake Road — possibly the original elementary campus, unverified. Lineage: Mark Twain Elementary School (Florissant; alumni site covers 'Classes of 1963-1981' and notes the school published only one yearbook, Spring 1974 — an unusual data point for Track B) → Mark Twain Student Support Center → Mark Twain Restoration and Re-Entry Center (renamed 2019 per Wikipedia FFSD) → Mark Twain Restoration & Wellness Center. Exact elementary opening and conversion dates not found; an FFSD board document (simbli.eboardsolutions.com) recently proposed restructuring/'Close Mark Twain Location', so current operating status should be re-verified before Track B.

name: Johnson-Wabash Elementary School
notes: Currently operating as Johnson-Wabash 6th Grade Center, 685 January Ave, Ferguson MO 63135 (jw.fergflor.org; NCES 291201002784 'Open' 2023-24). The name merges the earlier Johnson and Wabash schools (per seed historical names); the building sits on the same January Avenue block as Ferguson Middle (701 January). Neither the construction date nor the earlier Johnson/Wabash school histories were findable online. It was reconfigured from an elementary to a 6th-grade center in the ~2019 grade-center restructuring (Wikipedia FFSD school list) and is slated to return to K-5 in the district's 2027-28 restructuring (fergflor.org board post). Seed's 'serves portions of Berkeley' is plausible (Walnut Grove Primary explicitly lists Berkeley in its attendance communities) but boundary details unverified.

name: Walnut Grove Primary School
notes: Currently operating as Walnut Grove Primary School (PreK-2), 1248 North Florissant Road, Ferguson MO 63135, serving Berkeley, Calverton Park, Florissant, and Ferguson (wgps.fergflor.org; FFSD 2023-24 directory lists it as 'Walnut Grove Elementary'). Operating by 1973 at the latest — a Pacific Standard memoir describes attending Walnut Grove Elementary in 1973. Construction/opening date not found online; recommend DESE building records or district facilities documents for the exact year.

name: Airport Elementary School - Berkeley Community Center
district_operator: Berkeley School District (1954-1975); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (1975-2019); City of Berkeley (2023-)
notes: Recorded as the school entity (the relevant yearbook target): per the City of Berkeley's August 2023 RFP for conversion, 'Airport Elementary School and gymnasium were constructed on this site in 1954... The School was closed in 2019 due to declining enrollment, and the City purchased the property in 2023.' It operated as a Berkeley district school 1954-1975, then under Ferguson-Florissant until closure in the district's 2019 restructuring. The City of Berkeley bought the ~10.4-acre parcel (Bills #4957/#4965, 2023) and is converting it into the Berkeley Community Center — seed's 'Opened 2023' describes that conversion, not a school opening (seed status 'Converted' is accurate). Students were redistributed to other FFSD elementaries (Berkeley Elementary/Intermediate and Holman are the nearest); no single successor school documented. Duplicate of ALL-390 'Airport Elementary School - Historical Campus' in another batch — same building.

name: Robertson School District
district_operator: Robertson School District (to ~1964); Berkeley School District (1964-1975); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (after 1975)
notes: Probable reconstruction: Robertson was an unincorporated, predominantly Black community west of Lambert Field (post office 1929-1958, roadsidethoughts.com; an early-1800s French settlement that became a historic Black community, per Missouri Sen. Chappelle-Nadal's 2016 history project). When the Robertson high school closed in 1964, 'the Berkeley School District voluntarily provided school bus transportation and welcomed the Robertson students into their system' (Wikipedia 'Berkeley High School (Berkeley, Missouri)'). The district itself appears to have been absorbed into Berkeley around then: Robertson is absent from the 1975 court order (which addressed only Berkeley and Kinloch), yet an FFSD geographical study (studylib.net doc 7845312) places Robertson inside the post-merger district as a discontinuous western piece, and PRiME Center documents that most remaining small districts were annexed in the 1960s. Whether the annexation was formal in 1964 or was only a tuition/transport arrangement that later became a boundary change is unverified — recommend human follow-up with St. Louis County school district boundary records. Operated at least a high school (ALL-410) and an elementary-level school (ALL-411). The community was largely bought out/demolished for the Lambert W-1W runway expansion (1990s-2000s).

name: Robertson High School
district_operator: Robertson School District (to ~1964); students then bused to Berkeley School District
notes: Seed's 1964 closure corroborated: 'those circumstances changed in 1964 with the closure of the Robertson, Missouri high school, located in a predominantly African American community... the Berkeley School District voluntarily provided school bus transportation and welcomed the Robertson students into their system' (Wikipedia 'Berkeley High School (Berkeley, Missouri)' — probable, secondary). Consistent with former Robertson residents' accounts that 'our high school closed' amid the community's decline (Missouri Senate history project, 2016). Successor recorded as Berkeley High School (ALL-114, in another batch) since Robertson students were bused there. Opening date, building location, and whether it was a dedicated high school or a program within the Robertson school are all undetermined — nothing found via web search; likely requires county school records or the Kinloch/FFSD archives as a human follow-up.

name: Robertson Elementary School
district_operator: Robertson School District (to ~1964); Berkeley School District (~1964-1975); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (1975)
notes: Diverging from seed's 1964: an FFSD geographical study (studylib.net doc 7845312) states that as a result of the court-ordered desegregation 'all the schools in the Kinloch and Robertson areas were closed and all the Afro-American students who live there are bussed to schools in the northern part of the school district' — implying a Robertson-area school was still operating within the Berkeley district up to the 1975 merger and was closed afterward, with students bused north. Two readings: (a) seed's 1964 marks only the district/HS dissolution while the elementary continued under Berkeley until ~1975 (adopted here as the best-supported path); (b) the elementary also closed in 1964 and Robertson children were bused to Berkeley schools from then — the study's phrasing weighs against this but doesn't exclude it. Exact building/location never identified online; recommend human follow-up with FFSD records or St. Louis County plat/parish records (the community site was largely erased by the airport buyout).

name: Ferguson High School
district_operator: Ferguson Public School District (1939-1952); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (1952-1962)
notes: Seed confirmed. Ferguson High School opened in 1939 with 400 students transferred from John M. Vogt High School; built by the Ferguson Public School District on the January Estate ('Blizzard Hill', also the former city dump) at 701 January Ave with WPA assistance (Living New Deal; Wikipedia 'McCluer High School'; the school's own 1948 Crest yearbook history on e-yearbook.com recounts the Ferguson high-school lineage back to 1894). Last graduating class 1962 — students then moved to McCluer High School (ALL-111), which converted from junior high to senior high that year. The January Ave building continued as Ferguson Junior High (ALL-418), now Ferguson Middle School. Yearbook was 'The Crest' — the name inherited from Vogt High School's yearbook (begun 1931). OVERLAP FLAG: ALL-417 (January Avenue Campus) is the same school entity, kept separate per the no-merge rule.

name: Ferguson High School - January Avenue Campus
district_operator: Ferguson Public School District (1939-1952); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (1952-1962)
notes: OVERLAP FLAG: this is the same school entity as ALL-416 — the January Avenue building was Ferguson High School's only location, not a separate campus alongside others (unlike the Berkeley HS multi-campus rows). Flagged in data/schools_seed_deduped_review_needed.json; kept separate per the dedup rules and this task's no-silent-merge instruction, but a merge into ALL-416 should be considered in the coordinator pass. Same history: WPA-built 1939 on the January Estate, last graduating class 1962, students moved to McCluer (ALL-111), building became Ferguson Junior High then Ferguson Middle School (still operating). Yearbook: 'The Crest.'

name: Ferguson Junior High School
notes: Direct continuation of the Ferguson High School building at 701 January Ave after the 1962 high-school consolidation to McCluer — 'Ferguson High School's last graduating class was in 1962; with the school becoming Ferguson Junior High; now Ferguson Middle School' (Living New Deal). Still operating as Ferguson Middle School, 701 January Ave, Ferguson MO 63135 (fms.fergflor.org). The exact year of the junior-high-to-middle rename was not found online. OVERLAP FLAG: ALL-419 'Ferguson Middle School' (in another batch's seed) is the same continuous entity — this row and that row describe one school under two era names.
